India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.

Title: Disappointed with Lack of Discounts for Regular Blood Donations

However, despite my consistent efforts, I have never received any discounts on blood when I required it during my own medical emergencies. I find this disheartening, as it seems that ANVISHKA does not value the loyalty and dedication of the blood donors

It is not unreasonable to expect some form of acknowledgment or incentive for those of us who selflessly give our blood to help others. Other blood banks and organizations often provide discounts or priority access to regular donors, recognizing their commitment and encouraging them to continue their vital contributions.

I sincerely hope that ANVISHKA takes this feedback into consideration and reevaluates their policies regarding discounts for regular blood donors. Acknowledging and rewarding the generosity of individuals who consistently support their cause would not only foster a stronger bond with the donor community but also motivate others to become regular blood donors.

I still believe in the importance of blood donation and will continue to contribute to the cause, but I hope ANVISHKA reconsiders their stance on recognizing the dedication of their regular donors.

owner_posts.post_text:
The thyroid is a small, butterfly-shaped gland located at the base of the front of your neck, just below the Adam’s apple. It is a critical part of your endocrine system, acting as the body's "powerhouse" by producing hormones that regulate the speed of your metabolism—how your body transforms food into energy.

Core Functions : 
The thyroid produces two primary hormones, Thyroxine (T4) and Triiodothyronine (T3), which travel through the bloodstream to affect nearly every cell in the body. These hormones control

Energy Levels: Regulating how fast you burn calories.

Vital Signs: Influencing heart rate, blood pressure, and body temperature.

Growth & Development: Crucial for brain development in infants and physical growth in children.
Digestion: Affecting how fast food moves through the digestive tract.

Common Thyroid Disorders:
Thyroid disease occurs when the gland produces too much or too little hormone, or when physical growths develop.

Hypothyroidism (Underactive): The thyroid doesn't make enough hormone, slowing down body functions. Common symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, feeling cold, and depression.

Hyperthyroidism (Overactive): The thyroid makes too much hormone, speeding up body functions. Common symptoms include weight loss (despite increased appetite), rapid heart rate, anxiety, and heat sensitivity.

Goiter: An abnormal enlargement of the gland that may look like a lump in the neck.
